Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

1035	\section{Separatedness I: pullback along the projection is injective}
1036	
1037	The plus construction of the preceding sections is a legitimate computation of the \'etale
1038	sheafification only because \emph{one} plus suffices, and that rests on the relative Picard
1039	functor being separated for the \'etale topology. This section establishes the geometric heart
1040	of that separatedness: pullback of Picard classes along the projection
1041	\(\mathrm{pr} \colon C \otimes T \to T\) is \emph{injective}, for every test object \(T\).
1042	
1043	Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) which is proper,
1044	geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over \(k\). We recall from elsewhere in
1045	this project the definitional Picard layer on a scheme \(X\): a \emph{pointed cover}
1046	\(\mathcal U\) of \(X\) assigns to each point \(x \in X\) an open \(\mathcal U(x) \ni x\);
1047	pointed covers are ordered by pointwise inclusion (a \emph{refinement}
1048	\(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\)), with pointwise intersection as meet; a \emph{unit \v Cech
1049	\(1\)-cocycle} \(\gamma\) on \(\mathcal U\) assigns to each pair \(x,y\) a unit
1050	\(\gamma_{xy} \in \struct X(\mathcal U(x) \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) satisfying
1051	\(\gamma_{xy}\gamma_{yz} = \gamma_{xz}\) on triple intersections; \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\)
1052	is the group of such cocycles modulo coboundaries \((\delta\alpha)_{xy} =
1053	\alpha_x\alpha_y^{-1}\) for families of units \(\alpha_x \in
1054	\struct X(\mathcal U(x))^{\times}\); restriction along a refinement is a group homomorphism
1055	\(\check H^1(\mathcal U) \to \check H^1(\mathcal W)\); and the Picard group
1056	\(\Pic(X)\) is the colimit of the \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\) along the (directed) refinement
1057	order, with structure maps written \([\mathcal U, a] \in \Pic(X)\), and with contravariant
1058	pullback \(f^{*} \colon \Pic(Y) \to \Pic(X)\) along a morphism \(f \colon X \to Y\), computed
1059	by pulling back the cover pointwise and the cocycle by \(f^{\sharp}\).
1060	
1061	\begin{lemma}[Separation for unit sections]
1062	  \label{lem:units_separation}
1063	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq}
1064	  \leanok
1065	  Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(V \subseteq X\) open, and \((W_i)_{i \in I}\) a family of opens
1066	  with \(W_i \subseteq V\) and \(V \subseteq \bigcup_i W_i\). If two units
1067	  \(s, t \in \struct X(V)^{\times}\) satisfy \(s|_{W_i} = t|_{W_i}\) for all \(i\), then
1068	  \(s = t\).

1077	  \label{lem:units_gluing}
1078	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_unitsRestrict_eq}
1079	  \leanok

1082	  \(u_i \in \struct X(W_i)^{\times}\) with \(u_i|_{W_i \cap W_j} = u_j|_{W_i \cap W_j}\) for
1083	  all \(i,j\) glues to a unit \(s \in \struct X(V)^{\times}\) with \(s|_{W_i} = u_i\).

1109	  \label{thm:unitsRes_injective}
1110	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRes_injective}
1111	  \leanok
1112	  Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\) pointed covers of \(X\). Then
1113	  restriction \(\check H^1(\mathcal U) \to \check H^1(\mathcal W)\) is injective.

1117	  \uses{lem:units_separation, lem:units_gluing, lem:unitsRestrict_trans}
1118	  Restriction is a group homomorphism, so it suffices to show a cocycle \(\gamma\) on
1119	  \(\mathcal U\) whose restriction to \(\mathcal W\) is a coboundary, say
1120	  \(\gamma_{zz'}|_{\mathcal W(z) \cap \mathcal W(z')} = \alpha_z \alpha_{z'}^{-1}\) with
1121	  \(\alpha_z \in \struct X(\mathcal W(z))^{\times}\), is itself a coboundary. Fix a point
1122	  \(i\) and consider, for each point \(z\), the \emph{comparison unit}
1123	  \[ s_{i,z} := \alpha_z \cdot \gamma_{iz}^{-1}
1124	     \in \struct X\bigl(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)\bigr)^{\times}, \]
1125	  which makes sense since \(\mathcal W(z) \subseteq \mathcal U(z)\). On the overlap
1126	  \((\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)) \cap (\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z'))\) the cocycle
1127	  identity \(\gamma_{iz}\gamma_{zz'} = \gamma_{iz'}\) at \((i,z,z')\) and the coboundary
1128	  relation \(\alpha_z \gamma_{zz'} = \alpha_{z'}\) give
1129	  \(s_{i,z'} = \alpha_z\gamma_{zz'}\cdot(\gamma_{iz}\gamma_{zz'})^{-1} = s_{i,z}\). Since
1130	  every point \(w \in \mathcal U(i)\) lies in \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(w)\), these
1131	  opens cover \(\mathcal U(i)\), and by gluing (Lemma~\ref{lem:units_gluing}) there is
1132	  \(\beta_i \in \struct X(\mathcal U(i))^{\times}\) with
1133	  \(\beta_i|_{\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal W(z)} = s_{i,z}\) for all \(z\). Finally, for any
1134	  \(i, j\), on each member \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j) \cap \mathcal W(z)\) of a cover
1135	  of \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j)\) we compute, using the cocycle identity at
1136	  \((i,j,z)\),
1137	  \[ \beta_i \gamma_{ij} = \alpha_z \gamma_{iz}^{-1}\gamma_{ij}
1138	       = \alpha_z \gamma_{jz}^{-1} = \beta_j , \]
1139	  so \(\beta_i \gamma_{ij} = \beta_j\) on \(\mathcal U(i) \cap \mathcal U(j)\) by separation
1140	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:units_separation}); that is, \(\gamma = \delta(\beta^{-1})\) is a
1141	  coboundary.

1190	  Every pointed cover of a scheme admits a refinement all of whose members are affine open.

1198	\begin{theorem}[Sections over an affine open pull back bijectively]
1199	  \label{thm:isIso_appLE_snd}
1200	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isIso_appLE_snd}
1201	  \leanok
1202	  Let \(T\) be an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) and \(V \subseteq T\) an affine open. Then
1203	  pullback of sections along the second projection
1204	  \(\mathrm{pr} \colon C \otimes T \to T\) is an isomorphism
1205	  \[ \Gamma(T, V) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \Gamma\bigl(C \otimes T,\
1206	     \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V\bigr). \]
1207	\end{theorem}
1208	\begin{proof}
1209	  \leanok
1210	  \uses{lem:flat_of_field, cor:curve_sections}
1211	  The underlying scheme of \(C \otimes T\) is the fibre product
1212	  \(C \times_{\Spec k} T\). Since \(C\) is proper over the field \(k\), its underlying space
1213	  is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and \(T \to \Spec k\) is flat
1214	  (Lemma~\ref{lem:flat_of_field}); therefore the canonical square of section rings
1215	  \[ \begin{array}{ccc}
1216	     \Gamma(\Spec k, \struct{}) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma(C, \struct C) \\
1217	     \downarrow & & \downarrow \\
1218	     \Gamma(T, V) & \longrightarrow & \Gamma(C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V)
1219	     \end{array} \]
1220	  --- with the affine slots at \(\Spec k\) (all of it) and at \(V \subseteq T\), and the
1221	  quasi-compact quasi-separated slot at all of \(C\) --- is a pushout of commutative rings:
1222	  the flat-base-change theorem for sections of fibre products. The top edge is an
1223	  isomorphism, \(\Gamma(C, \struct C) = k\) (Corollary~\ref{cor:curve_sections}); a pushout
1224	  of an isomorphism is an isomorphism, so the bottom edge is one too.
1225	\end{proof}

1228	  \label{cor:appLE_snd_injective}
1229	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Over.appLE_snd_injective}
1230	  \leanok
1231	  Let \(T\) be an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) and \(W \subseteq T\) any open. Then pullback
1232	  of sections along the second projection,
1233	  \(\Gamma(T, W) \to \Gamma(C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}W)\), is injective.
1234	\end{corollary}

1236	  \leanok
1237	  \uses{thm:isIso_appLE_snd}
1238	  Let \(s, t \in \Gamma(T,W)\) have equal pullbacks. For every affine open \(V \subseteq W\),
1239	  restriction to \(\mathrm{pr}^{-1}V\) followed by the bijection of
1240	  Theorem~\ref{thm:isIso_appLE_snd} shows \(s|_V = t|_V\); the affine opens contained in
1241	  \(W\) cover \(W\), so \(s = t\) by separation for \(\struct T\).
1242	\end{proof}

1245	  \label{cor:unitsAppLE_snd_bijective}

1247	  \leanok
1248	  Let \(T\) be an object of \(\Over(\Spec k)\) and \(V \subseteq T\) an affine open. Then

1250	  \(\Gamma(T, V)^{\times} \to \Gamma(C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V)^{\times}\) of unit
1251	  groups.
1252	\end{corollary}
1253	\begin{proof}
1254	  \leanok
1255	  \uses{thm:isIso_appLE_snd, cor:appLE_snd_injective}

1257	  (Corollary~\ref{cor:appLE_snd_injective}). For surjectivity, a unit
1258	  \(y \in \Gamma(C \otimes T, \mathrm{pr}^{-1}V)^{\times}\) and its inverse are pullbacks of
1259	  sections \(a, b \in \Gamma(T,V)\) by Theorem~\ref{thm:isIso_appLE_snd}; the products
1260	  \(ab\) and \(ba\) pull back to \(1\), hence equal \(1\) by injectivity, so \(a\) is a unit
1261	  pulling back to \(y\).

1264	\begin{lemma}[The projection is surjective]
1265	  \label{lem:surjective_snd}

1268	  For every object \(T\) of \(\Over(\Spec k)\), the second projection
1269	  \(C \otimes T \to T\) is surjective on points.

1272	  \leanok

1274	  particular nonempty, and \(\Spec k\) is a single point; so \(C \to \Spec k\) is
1275	  surjective. Surjectivity of morphisms of schemes is stable under base change, and the

1282	  \leanok
1283	  \source{kleiman-picard}

1291	    lem:unitsRestrict_trans}

1295	  with \(\mathcal U\) a pointed cover of \(T\) all of whose members \(\mathcal U(t)\) are

1297	  \(z \mapsto \mathrm{pr}^{-1}\mathcal U(\mathrm{pr}(z))\) by the pulled-back cocycle

1299	  Corollary~\ref{cor:cechPic_mk_eq_one}, \(\mathrm{pr}^{\sharp}\gamma\) is a coboundary
1300	  \emph{on the pulled-back cover itself}: there are units
1301	  \(w_z \in \struct{C \otimes T}(\mathrm{pr}^{-1}\mathcal U(\mathrm{pr} z))^{\times}\) with

9	/-!
10	# The transition cocycle of a locally trivialized module, and its Picard class
11	
12	Let `A` be a commutative ring, `N` an `A`-module, and `f : ι → A` a finite family with
13	localization models `S i`, `T i j`, `W i j k` away from the single, double and triple
14	products as in `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LocalizationCocycle`.  Given trivializations
15	`e i : S i ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[S i] S i` on the members of the cover, this file:
16	
17	* forms the **transition cocycle** `trivializationCocycle e i j : (T i j)ˣ` — the
18	  transition unit between the two pushforwards of `e i` and `e j` to the overlap — and
19	  shows it is a Čech cover cocycle (`isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle`), the diagonal
20	  and cocycle conditions being instances of the transition-unit calculus of
21	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.BaseChangeTrivialization` plus the uniqueness of `A`-algebra
22	  maps out of localizations;
23	* assembles the componentwise trivializations into one over the cover algebra
24	  `B := ∀ i, S i` (`Module.piTrivialization`);
25	* proves the **descent identification** (`picClass_trivializationCocycle`): the Picard
26	  class of the descent cocycle associated with the transition cocycle is the class of
27	  `N` itself.  The compatibility of the assembled trivialization with the twisted
28	  descent datum reduces, through the identification `B ⊗[A] B ≃ ∀ p, T p.1 p.2`, to the
29	  defining property of the transition units, and uniqueness of descent
30	  (`Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`) identifies the descended module with `N`.
31	
32	This is the algebraic heart of the surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism
33	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_surjective`).
34	-/

46	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]

49	`A`-algebras. -/
50	noncomputable def piBaseChangeDistrib :
51	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i ⊗[A] N :=
52	  (TensorProduct.comm A _ _).trans ((TensorProduct.piRight A A N S).trans
53	    (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ TensorProduct.comm A N (S i)))
54

56	lemma piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul (b : ∀ i, S i) (n : N) :
57	    piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S) (b ⊗ₜ[A] n) = fun i ↦ b i ⊗ₜ[A] n := by
58	  funext i
59	  simp [piBaseChangeDistrib, TensorProduct.piRight_apply]

61	variable (e : ∀ i, (S i ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[S i] S i)
62	
63	/-- The `A`-linear map underlying `piTrivialization`: `n ↦ (i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n))`. -/
64	private noncomputable def piTrivializationBase : N →ₗ[A] ∀ i, S i where
65	  toFun n i := e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)
66	  map_add' n m := by
67	    funext i
68	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add]
69	  map_smul' a n := by
70	    funext i
71	    simp only [RingHom.id_apply, Pi.smul_apply, TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
72	    exact LinearMapClass.map_smul_of_tower (e i) a _

75	into a trivialization over the product algebra, sending `1 ⊗ₜ n` to
76	`fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n)` (`piTrivialization_one_tmul`). -/
77	noncomputable def piTrivialization :
78	    ((∀ i, S i) ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[∀ i, S i] ∀ i, S i := by
79	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
80	    (LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e)) ?_
81	  have key : ⇑(LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e))
82	      = (fun v i ↦ e i (v i)) ∘ ⇑(piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)) := by
83	    funext x
84	    induction x with
85	    | zero => exact funext fun i ↦ by simp
86	    | tmul b n =>
87	        funext i
88	        simp only [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, Function.comp_apply,
89	          piBaseChangeDistrib_tmul]
90	        have hb : (b i ⊗ₜ[A] n : S i ⊗[A] N) = b i • ((1 : S i) ⊗ₜ[A] n) := by
91	          rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
92	        rw [hb, map_smul]
93	        simp [piTrivializationBase, smul_eq_mul]
94	    | add x y hx hy =>
95	        rw [map_add, hx, hy]
96	        funext i
97	        simp only [Function.comp_apply, map_add, Pi.add_apply]
98	  rw [key]
99	  exact ((Equiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ (e i).toEquiv).bijective).comp
100	    (piBaseChangeDistrib (S := S)).bijective
101

104	    piTrivialization e (1 ⊗ₜ n) = fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n) := by
105	  change LinearMap.liftBaseChange (∀ i, S i) (piTrivializationBase e) (1 ⊗ₜ n) = _
106	  rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
107	  rfl

201	    (isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit f S T W

218	    have hval : ψ (1 ⊗ₜ n) = fun i ↦ e i (1 ⊗ₜ n) := piTrivialization_one_tmul e n

9	# The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism of an affine scheme
10	
11	Assembly of the choice-independent Picard classes of
12	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine` into the injective group homomorphism
13	
14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
15	
16	for an affine scheme `X` — the homomorphism half of the Čech–Picard dictionary
17	(mathlib's `RingTheory.PicardGroup` TODO "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").
18	Injectivity (`CechPic.toPic_injective`) is refinement injectivity: a trivial descent
19	class makes the descent unit a coboundary, which glues back to a coboundary on the
20	pointed cover itself.  Surjectivity — trivializations of an invertible module on a basic
21	cover — is the remaining half of the dictionary.
22	-/
23	
24	set_option autoImplicit false
25	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
26	
27	universe u
28	
29	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
30	
31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
32	
33	namespace Scheme
34	
35	/-! ## The descent homomorphism -/
36	
37	namespace CechPic
38	
39	open PointedCover
40	
41	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
42	
43	/-- The underlying function of `CechPic.toPic`: descend along a chosen basic refinement
44	of a chosen representative. -/
45	noncomputable def toPicFun : X.CechPic → CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
46	  Quotient.lift
47	    (fun p : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 ↦
48	      (BasicRefinement.nonempty p.1).some.pic p.2.out)
49	    (by
50	      rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
51	      -- The restrictions of the chosen representatives to `𝒲` are cohomologous:
52	      -- their `H¹` classes are `unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b`.
53	      refine BasicRefinement.pic_congr h₁ h₂ _ _ ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ?_)
54	      have ha : a.out.class = a := Quot.out_eq a
55	      have hb : b.out.class = b := Quot.out_eq b
56	      calc (a.out.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h₁ x)).class
57	          = unitsRes h₁ a.out.class := rfl
58	        _ = unitsRes h₂ b.out.class := by rw [ha, hb]; exact e
59	        _ = (b.out.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h₂ x)).class := rfl)
60	
61	variable {X}
62	
63	@[simp]
64	lemma toPicFun_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
65	    (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) : toPicFun X (CechPic.mk 𝒰 γ.class) = P.pic γ := by
66	  -- The chosen data compare to `(P, γ)` by `BasicRefinement.pic_congr` with `𝒲 := 𝒰`
67	  -- (the representative `Quot.out (γ.class)` is cohomologous to `γ`).
68	  show (BasicRefinement.nonempty 𝒰).some.pic (Quot.out γ.class) = P.pic γ
69	  refine BasicRefinement.pic_congr (𝒲 := 𝒰) le_rfl le_rfl _ _
70	    ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ?_)
71	  have hγ : (Quot.out γ.class).class = γ.class := Quot.out_eq γ.class
72	  calc ((Quot.out γ.class).res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((le_rfl : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) x)).class
73	      = unitsRes le_rfl (Quot.out γ.class).class := rfl
74	    _ = unitsRes le_rfl γ.class := by rw [hγ]
75	    _ = (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((le_rfl : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) x)).class := rfl
76	
77	variable (X)
78	
79	/-- **The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism** of an affine scheme: from the definitional
80	Čech Picard group to mathlib's Picard group of the global sections, by faithfully flat
81	descent along finite basic covers. -/
82	noncomputable def toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) where
83	  toFun := toPicFun X
84	  map_one' := by
85	    have h : (1 : X.CechPic) = CechPic.mk ⊤ (OneCocycle.class 1) := rfl
86	    obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty (⊤ : X.PointedCover)
87	    rw [h, toPicFun_mk _ _ P]
88	    exact P.pic_one
89	  map_mul' x y := by
90	    induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
91	    induction y using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
92	    obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱)
93	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
94	    induction b using Quot.ind with | _ δ =>
95	    rw [CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf]
96	    have hprod : (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (Quot.mk _ γ)
97	          * unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒱) (Quot.mk _ δ) : X.unitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱))
98	        = ((γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) x))
99	            * (δ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE ((inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ≤ 𝒱) x))).class := rfl
100	    have h1 : (Quot.mk _ γ : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = γ.class := rfl
101	    have h2 : (Quot.mk _ δ : X.unitsH1 𝒱) = δ.class := rfl
102	    rw [hprod, h1, h2, toPicFun_mk _ _ P,
103	      toPicFun_mk _ _ (P.ofLE inf_le_left), toPicFun_mk _ _ (P.ofLE inf_le_right),
104	      BasicRefinement.pic_ofLE inf_le_left P γ, BasicRefinement.pic_ofLE inf_le_right P δ,
105	      BasicRefinement.pic_mul]
106	
107	variable {X}
108	
109	@[simp]
110	lemma toPic_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) :
111	    toPic X (CechPic.mk 𝒰 γ.class) = P.pic γ :=
112	  toPicFun_mk 𝒰 γ P
113	
114	/-- **Injectivity of the descent homomorphism**: refinement injectivity for the Čech
115	Picard group against mathlib's Picard group. -/
116	theorem toPic_injective : Function.Injective (toPic X) := by
117	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_one]
118	  intro x hx
119	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
120	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
121	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := BasicRefinement.nonempty 𝒰
122	  rw [show Quot.mk _ γ = OneCocycle.class γ from rfl] at hx ⊢
123	  rw [toPic_mk 𝒰 γ P] at hx
124	  rw [BasicRefinement.class_eq_one_of_pic_eq_one P γ hx]
125	  exact CechPic.mk_one 𝒰
126	
127	end CechPic

23	The route: an invertible module `N` over `Γ(X, ⊤)` trivializes on the basic open of
24	some section outside every prime, so the trivializing sections span the unit ideal
25	(`Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`) and their basic opens cover `X`.  A
26	choice of one trivializing basic neighborhood per point is a `TrivializingFamily`; the
27	transition units of its trivializations (`Module.transitionUnit`) form a unit Čech
28	cocycle on the associated pointed cover.  Along any finite basic refinement the
29	restricted cover cocycle is the transition cocycle of the pushed-forward
30	trivializations, so its descended module is `N` itself
31	(`IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle`), and `toPic` hits the class
32	of `N`.
33	-/

50	/-- A pointed trivializing family for a module `N` over the global sections of `X`: one
51	section per point, whose basic open contains the point and carries a trivialization of
52	the base change of `N`.  Invertible modules over affine schemes always admit one
53	(`TrivializingFamily.nonempty`). -/
54	structure TrivializingFamily (X : Scheme.{u}) (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
55	    [Module Γ(X, ⊤) N] : Type u where
56	  /-- The trivializing section at a point. -/
57	  sec : X → Γ(X, ⊤)
58	  /-- Each point lies in the basic open of its section. -/
59	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ x, x ∈ X.basicOpen (sec x)
60	  /-- The chosen trivialization of `N` over the basic open. -/
61	  triv : ∀ x, (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)
62	    ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))] Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))

68	/-- Every invertible module over the global sections of an affine scheme admits a
69	trivializing family: the trivializing sections span the unit ideal, so their basic
70	opens cover `X`. -/
71	theorem nonempty [IsAffine X] [Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) N] :
72	    Nonempty (TrivializingFamily X N) := by
73	  have hcover :
74	      (⨆ f : {f : Γ(X, ⊤) | ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) S],
75	          IsLocalization.Away f S → Module.Free S (S ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)},
76	        X.basicOpen f.1) = ⊤ :=
77	    (isAffineOpen_top X).iSup_basicOpen_eq_self_iff.mpr
78	      (Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top N)
79	  have hex : ∀ x : X, ∃ f : Γ(X, ⊤),
80	      (∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) S],
81	        IsLocalization.Away f S → Module.Free S (S ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N))
82	      ∧ x ∈ X.basicOpen f := by
83	    intro x
84	    obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (hcover.ge (trivial : x ∈ (⊤ : X.Opens)))
85	    exact ⟨f.1, f.2, hf⟩
86	  choose f hfree hmem using hex
87	  refine ⟨⟨f, hmem, fun x ↦ ?_⟩⟩
88	  haveI : Module.Free Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N) :=
89	    hfree x Γ(X, X.basicOpen (f x)) inferInstance
90	  exact (Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv.mp this).some

107	/-- The transition cocycle of the trivializing family: on each double overlap, the
108	transition unit between the pushforwards of the trivializations at the two points. -/
109	noncomputable def transition (x y : X) : Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))ˣ :=
110	  IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle F.sec
111	    (fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
112	    (fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) F.triv x y
113	
114	/-- The transition units form a Čech cover cocycle on the (infinite) family of
115	trivializing basic opens. -/
116	lemma isCoverCocycle_transition :
117	    IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
118	      (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
119	      (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
120	      (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))))
121	      F.transition :=
122	  IsLocalization.AwayCover.isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle F.sec _ _ _ F.triv
123	
124	/-- The cocycle identity for the transition units, restricted to any common open. -/
125	lemma transition_mul (x y z : X) {T : X.Opens}
126	    (hxy : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))
127	    (hyz : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec y * F.sec z))
128	    (hxz : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec z)) :
129	    X.unitsRestrict hxy (F.transition x y) * X.unitsRestrict hyz (F.transition y z)
130	      = X.unitsRestrict hxz (F.transition x z) := by
131	  -- restrictions from the double overlaps to the triple overlap
132	  have h₁₂ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
133	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y) :=
134	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec z, by ring⟩
135	  have h₂₃ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
136	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec y * F.sec z) :=
137	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec x, by ring⟩
138	  have h₁₃ : X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z))
139	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec z) :=
140	    X.basicOpen_le_of_dvd ⟨F.sec y, by ring⟩
141	  -- the common open sits inside the triple overlap
142	  have hT : T ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)) := by
143	    rw [X.basicOpen_mul, X.basicOpen_mul]
144	    exact le_inf (hxy.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_left))
145	      (le_inf (hxy.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right))
146	        (hyz.trans ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right)))
147	  -- the cover cocycle identity, with the face maps rewritten as restrictions
148	  have hc := (F.isCoverCocycle_transition).cocycle x y z
149	  rw [show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₂₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
150	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
151	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
152	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₂₃ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
153	    show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₂ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
154	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
155	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
156	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₁₂ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
157	    show IsLocalization.AwayCover.face₁₃ (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
158	        (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y)))
159	        (W := fun x y z ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * (F.sec y * F.sec z)))) x y z
160	      = X.basicRes _ _ h₁₃ from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _] at hc
161	  -- lift to units on the triple overlap
162	  have hu : X.unitsRestrict h₂₃ (F.transition y z) * X.unitsRestrict h₁₂ (F.transition x y)
163	      = X.unitsRestrict h₁₃ (F.transition x z) := Units.ext hc
164	  -- restrict to `T` and collapse the composed restrictions
165	  have e := congrArg (X.unitsRestrict hT) hu
166	  rw [map_mul, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
167	    unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e
168	  exact (mul_comm _ _).trans e

170	/-- The unit Čech cocycle of a trivializing family on its pointed cover: the value on
171	`T ≤ D(sec x) ⊓ D(sec y)` is the restriction of the transition unit. -/
172	noncomputable def cocycle : X.unitsCocycle F.cover where
173	  ev x y _ a b :=
174	    X.unitsRestrict ((le_inf a.le b.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge)
175	      (F.transition x y)
176	  ev_precomp _ _ _ _ _ _ _ := unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict _ _ _
177	  ev_trans x y z _ a b c :=
178	    F.transition_mul x y z
179	      ((le_inf a.le b.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge)
180	      ((le_inf b.le c.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec y) (F.sec z)).ge)
181	      ((le_inf a.le c.le).trans (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec z)).ge)
182	
183	/-- The pair values of the trivializing cocycle are the restricted transition units. -/
184	lemma cocycle_unitsEvInf (x y : X) :
185	    unitsEvInf F.cocycle x y
186	      = X.unitsRestrict (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec x) (F.sec y)).ge (F.transition x y) :=
187	  rfl

190	
191	/-- The trivializations of the family, pushed forward to a basic refinement of the
192	trivializing cover. -/
193	noncomputable def refTriv (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) (i : P.ι) :
194	    (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)
195	      ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i))] Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)) :=
196	  Module.trivializationPush (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le i)) (F.triv (P.pt i))
197	
198	/-- Restricting the trivializing cocycle to a basic refinement recovers the transition
199	cocycle of the pushed trivializations. -/
200	lemma coverCocycle_eq (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) (i j : P.ι) :
201	    P.coverCocycle F.cocycle i j
202	      = IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle P.r
203	          (fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
204	          (fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) (F.refTriv P) i j := by
205	  have hle : X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j)
206	      ≤ X.basicOpen (F.sec (P.pt i) * F.sec (P.pt j)) :=
207	    (P.overlap_le i j).trans (X.basicOpen_mul _ _).ge
208	  have h₁ : P.coverCocycle F.cocycle i j
209	      = X.unitsRestrict hle (F.transition (P.pt i) (P.pt j)) :=
210	    unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict (X.basicOpen_mul (F.sec (P.pt i)) (F.sec (P.pt j))).ge
211	      (P.overlap_le i j) (F.transition (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
212	  rw [h₁, IsLocalization.AwayCover.trivializationCocycle, refTriv, refTriv,
213	    Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
214	    Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
215	    show (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
216	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
217	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j).comp
218	          (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le i))
219	      = (X.basicRes _ _ hle).comp
220	          (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
221	            (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
222	            (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
223	      from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
224	    show (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)
225	        (S := fun i ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i)))
226	        (T := fun i j ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * P.r j))) i j).comp
227	          (X.basicRes _ _ (P.basicOpen_le j))
228	      = (X.basicRes _ _ hle).comp
229	          (IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclRight (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := F.sec)
230	            (S := fun x ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x)))
231	            (T := fun x y ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (F.sec x * F.sec y))) (P.pt i) (P.pt j))
232	      from X.basicOpen_algHom_ext _ _ _,
233	    ← Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
234	    ← Module.trivializationPush_trivializationPush,
235	    Module.map_transitionUnit]
236	  rfl

238	/-- **Descent identification**: along any basic refinement, the Picard class of the
239	trivializing cocycle is the class of `N` itself. -/
240	theorem pic_cocycle [Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) N] (P : F.cover.BasicRefinement) :
241	    P.pic F.cocycle = CommRing.Pic.mk Γ(X, ⊤) N := by
242	  letI := P.faithfullyFlat
243	  rw [P.pic_eq_picClass]
244	  refine (Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_congr _
245	      (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit _ _ _
246	        (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
247	        (IsLocalization.AwayCover.isCoverCocycle_trivializationCocycle P.r _ _
248	          (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k))))
249	          (F.refTriv P)))
250	      (congrArg _ (funext fun i ↦ funext fun j ↦ F.coverCocycle_eq P i j))).trans
251	    (IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle P.r _ _
252	      (fun i j k ↦ Γ(X, X.basicOpen (P.r i * (P.r j * P.r k)))) (F.refTriv P))

270	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := PointedCover.BasicRefinement.nonempty F.cover

272	  rw [toPic_mk F.cover F.cocycle P, F.pic_cocycle P, CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_self]

9	/-!
10	# The Čech–Picard dictionary for affine schemes: the descent homomorphism
11	
12	For an affine scheme `X`, this file assembles the Picard classes of unit Čech cocycles
13	along basic refinements (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffineCover`) into an injective
14	group homomorphism
15	
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
17	
18	from the definitional Čech Picard group into mathlib's Picard group of the global
19	sections.  (Surjectivity — hence the full dictionary `X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
20	— is the invertible-module-trivialization direction, treated separately.)
21	
22	The core is the **independence of the descent Picard class from every choice**
23	(`BasicRefinement.pic_congr`): representing cocycle of the `H¹` class, basic refinement,
24	and pointed cover.  All comparisons are routed through three elementary moves:
25	
26	* `pic_res` — replacing the pointed cover by a finer one and restricting the cocycle
27	  does not change the refinement data nor the class (the restricted evaluations agree on
28	  the nose);
29	* `pic_eq_of_isCohomologous` — cohomologous cocycles give equal classes (the comparison
30	  restricts to an index-wise coboundary; coboundary invariance of the descended module);
31	* `pic_interFst` / `pic_inter` / `pic_interFst_eq_inter` — any two basic refinements of
32	  the same cover are dominated by their merge, on which the two point-selections differ
33	  by the index-wise coboundary of the cross evaluations `γ (pt i, pt' j)`; hence all
34	  refinements give the same class.
35	
36	Injectivity is refinement injectivity: a trivial descent class makes the descent unit a
37	coboundary (`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_eq_one_iff`), whose components glue back to
38	a coboundary on the pointed cover itself
39	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family`).
40	-/

91	back does not change the Picard class: the two cover cocycles agree on the nose. -/
92	theorem pic_ofLE (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (P : 𝒱.BasicRefinement) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
93	    (P.ofLE h).pic γ = P.pic (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)) := by
94	  -- Both sides are `picClass` of `isDescentCocycle_cocycleUnit` for the same data:
95	  -- `coverCocycle` of the restricted cocycle is the composed restriction of the same
96	  -- evaluations.
97	  have hcc : (P.ofLE h).coverCocycle γ = P.coverCocycle (γ.res fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)) := by
98	    funext i j
99	    rw [coverCocycle, coverCocycle, res_unitsEvInf h γ, unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict]
100	    rfl
101	  haveI := (P.ofLE h).faithfullyFlat
102	  haveI := P.faithfullyFlat

108	/-- Cohomologous unit cocycles have the same Picard class along any basic refinement. -/
109	theorem pic_eq_of_isCohomologous (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) {γ γ' : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
110	    (h : γ.IsCohomologous γ') : P.pic γ = P.pic γ' := by
111	  letI := P.faithfullyFlat
112	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp h
113	  -- restate the comparison through the `Γ`-typed interface
114	  have hα' : ∀ z w : X,
115	      X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens w ≤ 𝒰.opens z) (α z)
116	          * unitsEvInf γ z w
117	        = unitsEvInf γ' z w
118	          * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : 𝒰.opens z ⊓ 𝒰.opens w ≤ 𝒰.opens w) (α w) :=
119	    fun z w ↦ hα z w
120	  have hrel : ∀ i j, (P.coverCocycle γ i j).val
121	      = IsLocalization.AwayCover.inclLeft (A := Γ(X, ⊤)) (f := P.r)

\section{The \v Cech--Picard dictionary}

For a commutative ring \(A\), write \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\) for its \emph{module} Picard
group: the group, under \(\otimes_A\), of isomorphism classes of invertible \(A\)-modules
--- those \(A\)-modules \(N\) admitting an \(A\)-module \(N'\) with \(N \otimes_A N' \cong A\).
This section identifies, for an affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A := \Gamma(X,\struct
X)\), the \v Cech Picard group \(\Pic(X)\) recalled at the head of the previous section ---
the colimit of the groups \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\) of unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycles on pointed
covers \(\mathcal U\) of \(X\) --- with \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\).

For \(f \in A\), write \(D(f) \subseteq X\) for its basic open, the largest open on which the
image of \(f\) in every stalk is a unit; \(D(f) \cap D(g) = D(fg)\), and, \(X\) being affine, a
family \((D(f))_{f \in S}\) covers \(X\) exactly when \(S\) generates the unit ideal of \(A\).
A \emph{finite basic refinement} of a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\) is a finite pointed cover
\(\mathcal W\) refining \(\mathcal U\) all of whose members are basic opens \(D(r_i)\),
\(i \in I\), of elements \(r_i \in A\); since \(X\) is quasi-compact, being affine, every
pointed cover admits one. A unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle \(\delta\) on such a \(\mathcal W\)
determines a \emph{descent datum} for the finite faithfully flat algebra
\(A \to \prod_{i \in I} \Gamma(X, D(r_i))\), by twisting the tautological gluing data of the
free rank-one modules \(\Gamma(X,D(r_i))\) by the transition units \(\delta_{ij}\); faithfully
flat descent produces from this datum an \(A\)-module, well defined up to isomorphism, the
\emph{module descended from \(\delta\)}.

\begin{theorem}[Trivializing elements span the unit ideal]
  \label{thm:invertible_span_free}
  \lean{Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top}
  \leanok
  Let \(A\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) an invertible \(A\)-module. The ideal generated by
  \[
    \{\, f \in A : S \otimes_A N \text{ is a free } S\text{-module for every localization } S
    \text{ of } A \text{ away from } f \,\}
  \]
  is the unit ideal of \(A\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  An invertible module is finitely presented, and for every prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\) of
  \(A\) the localization of \(N\) at \(\mathfrak p\) is a finite flat module over the local
  ring \(A_{\mathfrak p}\), hence free; by finite presentation, freeness at \(\mathfrak p\)
  spreads out to freeness of \(S \otimes_A N\) for \(S\) a localization away from some single
  element \(f \notin \mathfrak p\). If the ideal generated by all such \(f\) were proper, it
  would be contained in some maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), contradicting the existence of a
  trivializing element outside \(\mathfrak m\). Hence the ideal is all of \(A\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Existence of a trivializing family]
  \label{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.nonempty}
  \uses{thm:invertible_span_free}
  \leanok
  Let \(X\) be an affine scheme with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\) and \(N\) an
  invertible \(A\)-module. There exists a \emph{trivializing family} for \(N\): an assignment,
  to each point \(x \in X\), of a section \(s_x \in A\) with \(x \in D(s_x)\), together with a
  trivialization
  \[
    \Gamma(X,D(s_x)) \otimes_A N \;\cong\; \Gamma(X,D(s_x))
  \]
  of the base change of \(N\) to \(D(s_x)\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  By Theorem~\ref{thm:invertible_span_free} the elements \(f \in A\) over which \(N\) becomes
  free after localizing away from \(f\) generate the unit ideal, so their basic opens \(D(f)\)
  cover \(X\). For each point \(x \in X\) choose one such \(f\) with \(x \in D(f)\) and set
  \(s_x := f\), together with the resulting trivialization of \(\Gamma(X,D(s_x)) \otimes_A
  N\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The cocycle of a trivializing family]
  \label{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.cocycle}
  \uses{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}
  \leanok
  Let \(F = (s_x, \mathrm{triv}_x)_{x \in X}\) be a trivializing family for \(N\) as in
  Lemma~\ref{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}, and let \(\mathcal U_F(x) := D(s_x)\) be the
  associated pointed cover. For points \(x,y \in X\), pushing \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) and
  \(\mathrm{triv}_y\) forward along the restriction maps to \(D(s_xs_y) = \mathcal U_F(x) \cap
  \mathcal U_F(y)\) produces two trivializations of \(N\) over \(D(s_xs_y)\); their
  \emph{transition unit} is the unique unit \(\gamma_{xy} \in \Gamma(X,D(s_xs_y))^{\times}\)
  with
  \[
    \gamma_{xy} \cdot \bigl(\text{pushforward of } \mathrm{triv}_x\bigr)(1 \otimes n) =
    \bigl(\text{pushforward of } \mathrm{triv}_y\bigr)(1 \otimes n) \qquad \text{for all } n \in
    N.
  \]
  The assignment \((x,y) \mapsto \gamma_{xy}\) is a unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle on
  \(\mathcal U_F\).
\end{definition}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  The diagonal identity \(\gamma_{xx} = 1\) holds because the two pushforwards of
  \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) to \(D(s_x^2)\) coincide, both being the unique \(A\)-algebra
  homomorphism out of the localization \(\Gamma(X,D(s_x))\) composed with \(\mathrm{triv}_x\).
  For the cocycle identity, push the trivializations \(\mathrm{triv}_x, \mathrm{triv}_y,
  \mathrm{triv}_z\) of a triple \(x,y,z\) forward to the triple overlap \(D(s_xs_ys_z)\): since
  the transition unit between two trivializations composes along a chain of further
  pushforwards --- pushing \(\gamma_{xy}\) and \(\gamma_{yz}\) both forward to
  \(D(s_xs_ys_z)\) compares \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) to \(\mathrm{triv}_y\) and \(\mathrm{triv}_y\)
  to \(\mathrm{triv}_z\) there --- their product equals the transition unit comparing
  \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) directly to \(\mathrm{triv}_z\), which restricts to \(\gamma_{xz}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Descent identification for the trivializing cocycle]
  \label{thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.pic_cocycle}
  \uses{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}
  \leanok
  In the situation of Definition~\ref{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}, let \(\mathcal W \le
  \mathcal U_F\) be any finite basic refinement of the trivializing cover. Then the class in
  \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\) of the module descended from the cocycle \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\)
  obtained by restricting the trivializing cocycle to \(\mathcal W\) equals the class of \(N\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Write \(\mathcal W(i) = D(r_i)\), \(i \in I\), with \(r_i\) a multiple of \(s_{p(i)}\) for a
  chosen point \(p(i)\) with \(\mathcal W(i) \subseteq \mathcal U_F(p(i))\). Restricting a
  transition unit is compatible with pushing forward its defining trivializations further, so
  the restricted cocycle \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) is exactly the transition cocycle, on
  \(\mathcal W\), of the trivializations of \(N\) obtained by pushing \(\mathrm{triv}_{p(i)}\)
  forward from \(D(s_{p(i)})\) to \(D(r_i)\) for each \(i\). These pushed-forward
  trivializations assemble into one trivialization of \(N\) over the cover algebra
  \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i))\), and it intertwines the descent datum twisted by
  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) with the canonical descent datum of \(N\) base-changed to the cover
  algebra, by the defining property of the transition units on each factor of the twisted
  double-overlap algebra \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i)) \otimes_A \prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i))\). Since
  the cover algebra is faithfully flat over \(A\) (a finite family of basic opens covering the
  affine \(X\)), uniqueness of descended modules identifies the module descended from
  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) with \(N\) itself, so their classes in \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\)
  agree.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The \v Cech--Picard descent homomorphism]
  \label{def:cechPic_toPic}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic}
  \leanok
  For an affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\), the homomorphism of
  groups
  \[
    \operatorname{toPic} \colon \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A), \qquad [\mathcal U,\gamma]
    \mapsto \bigl(\text{class of the module descended from } \gamma|_{\mathcal W}\bigr),
  \]
  where \(\mathcal W\) is any finite basic refinement of \(\mathcal U\) and
  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) is the cocycle obtained by restricting \(\gamma\) along
  \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\).
\end{definition}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  The class of the descended module does not depend on the choice of finite basic refinement
  \(\mathcal W\) of \(\mathcal U\): any two such refinements are dominated by a common one, along
  which the two descended modules become identified. Nor does it depend on the representative
  \((\mathcal U,\gamma)\) of the class \([\mathcal U,\gamma] \in \Pic(X)\): a further common
  refinement of two cohomologous representing cocycles carries cohomologous restricted
  cocycles, hence isomorphic descended modules. So \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is a well-defined
  function; it is a homomorphism because descending along a common refinement is compatible
  with the pointwise product of cocycles and with tensor product of the descended modules.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the descent homomorphism]
  \label{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_injective}
  \uses{def:cechPic_toPic, cor:cechPic_mk_eq_one}
  \leanok
  For every affine scheme \(X\), the descent homomorphism \(\operatorname{toPic} \colon
  \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) of Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic} is injective.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  It suffices to show that a class \([\mathcal U,\gamma]\) with
  \(\operatorname{toPic}[\mathcal U,\gamma] = 1\) is itself trivial. Represent
  \([\mathcal U,\gamma]\) along a finite basic refinement \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\) as in
  Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic}: since the module descended from \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\)
  is isomorphic to \(A\), its twisted descent datum is isomorphic to the trivial descent datum
  on \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,\mathcal W(i))\), so the transition units of \(\gamma\) restricted to
  \(\mathcal W\) differ from those of the trivial cocycle by an index-wise coboundary. Since the
  opens of \(\mathcal W\) refine those of \(\mathcal U\) and, member by member, cover them, this
  coboundary glues, by the sheaf property of \(\struct X\), to a coboundary for \(\gamma\)
  itself on \(\mathcal U\): \(\gamma = 1\) in \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\). By
  Corollary~\ref{cor:cechPic_mk_eq_one}, \([\mathcal U,\gamma] = 1\) in \(\Pic(X)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Surjectivity of the descent homomorphism]
  \label{thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_surjective}
  \uses{def:cechPic_toPic, lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty, thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}
  \leanok
  For every affine scheme \(X\), the descent homomorphism \(\operatorname{toPic} \colon
  \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) is surjective.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Let \(c \in \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) be represented by an invertible \(A\)-module \(N\). By
  Lemma~\ref{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}, \(N\) admits a trivializing family, giving a
  pointed cover \(\mathcal U_F\) together with the unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle \(\gamma_F\) of
  Definition~\ref{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}. Since \(X\) is affine, hence quasi-compact,
  \(\mathcal U_F\) admits a finite basic refinement \(\mathcal W\). By
  Theorem~\ref{thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}, \(\operatorname{toPic}[\mathcal
  U_F,\gamma_F] = c\). As \(c\) was arbitrary, \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is surjective.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The \v Cech--Picard dictionary]
  \label{thm:cechPicEquivPic}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic}
  \uses{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective, thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective}
  \leanok
  For every affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\), the descent
  homomorphism of Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic} is an isomorphism of groups
  \[
    \operatorname{toPic} \colon \Pic(X) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \operatorname{Pic}(A).
  \]
  In particular the definitional \v Cech Picard group \(\Pic(X)\) on pointed Zariski covers of
  \(X\) is canonically isomorphic to mathlib's Picard group of invertible \(A\)-modules.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is a bijective group homomorphism by
  Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective} (injectivity) and
  Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective} (surjectivity), hence an isomorphism.
\end{proof}

1331	A \emph{finite basic refinement} of a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\) is a finite pointed cover
1332	\(\mathcal W\) refining \(\mathcal U\) all of whose members are basic opens \(D(r_i)\),
1333	\(i \in I\), of elements \(r_i \in A\); since \(X\) is quasi-compact, being affine, every
1334	pointed cover admits one. A unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle \(\delta\) on such a \(\mathcal W\)
1335	determines a \emph{descent datum} for the finite faithfully flat algebra
1336	\(A \to \prod_{i \in I} \Gamma(X, D(r_i))\), by twisting the tautological gluing data of the
1337	free rank-one modules \(\Gamma(X,D(r_i))\) by the transition units \(\delta_{ij}\); faithfully
1338	flat descent produces from this datum an \(A\)-module, well defined up to isomorphism, the
1339	\emph{module descended from \(\delta\)}.

1341	\begin{theorem}[Trivializing elements span the unit ideal]
1342	  \label{thm:invertible_span_free}
1343	  \lean{Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top}
1344	  \leanok
1345	  Let \(A\) be a commutative ring and \(N\) an invertible \(A\)-module. The ideal generated by
1346	  \[
1347	    \{\, f \in A : S \otimes_A N \text{ is a free } S\text{-module for every localization } S
1348	    \text{ of } A \text{ away from } f \,\}
1349	  \]
1350	  is the unit ideal of \(A\).
1351	\end{theorem}
1352	\begin{proof}
1353	  \leanok
1354	  An invertible module is finitely presented, and for every prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\) of
1355	  \(A\) the localization of \(N\) at \(\mathfrak p\) is a finite flat module over the local
1356	  ring \(A_{\mathfrak p}\), hence free; by finite presentation, freeness at \(\mathfrak p\)
1357	  spreads out to freeness of \(S \otimes_A N\) for \(S\) a localization away from some single
1358	  element \(f \notin \mathfrak p\). If the ideal generated by all such \(f\) were proper, it
1359	  would be contained in some maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), contradicting the existence of a
1360	  trivializing element outside \(\mathfrak m\). Hence the ideal is all of \(A\).
1361	\end{proof}

1363	\begin{lemma}[Existence of a trivializing family]
1364	  \label{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}
1365	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.nonempty}
1366	  \uses{thm:invertible_span_free}
1367	  \leanok
1368	  Let \(X\) be an affine scheme with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\) and \(N\) an
1369	  invertible \(A\)-module. There exists a \emph{trivializing family} for \(N\): an assignment,
1370	  to each point \(x \in X\), of a section \(s_x \in A\) with \(x \in D(s_x)\), together with a
1371	  trivialization
1372	  \[
1373	    \Gamma(X,D(s_x)) \otimes_A N \;\cong\; \Gamma(X,D(s_x))
1374	  \]
1375	  of the base change of \(N\) to \(D(s_x)\).
1376	\end{lemma}
1377	\begin{proof}
1378	  \leanok
1379	  By Theorem~\ref{thm:invertible_span_free} the elements \(f \in A\) over which \(N\) becomes
1380	  free after localizing away from \(f\) generate the unit ideal, so their basic opens \(D(f)\)
1381	  cover \(X\). For each point \(x \in X\) choose one such \(f\) with \(x \in D(f)\) and set
1382	  \(s_x := f\), together with the resulting trivialization of \(\Gamma(X,D(s_x)) \otimes_A
1383	  N\).
1384	\end{proof}

1386	\begin{definition}[The cocycle of a trivializing family]
1387	  \label{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}
1388	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.cocycle}
1389	  \uses{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}
1390	  \leanok
1391	  Let \(F = (s_x, \mathrm{triv}_x)_{x \in X}\) be a trivializing family for \(N\) as in
1392	  Lemma~\ref{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}, and let \(\mathcal U_F(x) := D(s_x)\) be the
1393	  associated pointed cover. For points \(x,y \in X\), pushing \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) and
1394	  \(\mathrm{triv}_y\) forward along the restriction maps to \(D(s_xs_y) = \mathcal U_F(x) \cap
1395	  \mathcal U_F(y)\) produces two trivializations of \(N\) over \(D(s_xs_y)\); their
1396	  \emph{transition unit} is the unique unit \(\gamma_{xy} \in \Gamma(X,D(s_xs_y))^{\times}\)
1397	  with
1398	  \[
1399	    \gamma_{xy} \cdot \bigl(\text{pushforward of } \mathrm{triv}_x\bigr)(1 \otimes n) =
1400	    \bigl(\text{pushforward of } \mathrm{triv}_y\bigr)(1 \otimes n) \qquad \text{for all } n \in
1401	    N.
1402	  \]
1403	  The assignment \((x,y) \mapsto \gamma_{xy}\) is a unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle on
1404	  \(\mathcal U_F\).
1405	\end{definition}
1406	\begin{proof}
1407	  \leanok
1408	  The diagonal identity \(\gamma_{xx} = 1\) holds because the two pushforwards of
1409	  \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) to \(D(s_x^2)\) coincide, both being the unique \(A\)-algebra
1410	  homomorphism out of the localization \(\Gamma(X,D(s_x))\) composed with \(\mathrm{triv}_x\).
1411	  For the cocycle identity, push the trivializations \(\mathrm{triv}_x, \mathrm{triv}_y,
1412	  \mathrm{triv}_z\) of a triple \(x,y,z\) forward to the triple overlap \(D(s_xs_ys_z)\): since
1413	  the transition unit between two trivializations composes along a chain of further
1414	  pushforwards --- pushing \(\gamma_{xy}\) and \(\gamma_{yz}\) both forward to
1415	  \(D(s_xs_ys_z)\) compares \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) to \(\mathrm{triv}_y\) and \(\mathrm{triv}_y\)
1416	  to \(\mathrm{triv}_z\) there --- their product equals the transition unit comparing
1417	  \(\mathrm{triv}_x\) directly to \(\mathrm{triv}_z\), which restricts to \(\gamma_{xz}\).
1418	\end{proof}

1420	\begin{theorem}[Descent identification for the trivializing cocycle]
1421	  \label{thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}
1422	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.TrivializingFamily.pic_cocycle}
1423	  \uses{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}
1424	  \leanok
1425	  In the situation of Definition~\ref{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}, let \(\mathcal W \le
1426	  \mathcal U_F\) be any finite basic refinement of the trivializing cover. Then the class in
1427	  \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\) of the module descended from the cocycle \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\)
1428	  obtained by restricting the trivializing cocycle to \(\mathcal W\) equals the class of \(N\).
1429	\end{theorem}
1430	\begin{proof}
1431	  \leanok
1432	  Write \(\mathcal W(i) = D(r_i)\), \(i \in I\), with \(r_i\) a multiple of \(s_{p(i)}\) for a
1433	  chosen point \(p(i)\) with \(\mathcal W(i) \subseteq \mathcal U_F(p(i))\). Restricting a
1434	  transition unit is compatible with pushing forward its defining trivializations further, so
1435	  the restricted cocycle \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) is exactly the transition cocycle, on
1436	  \(\mathcal W\), of the trivializations of \(N\) obtained by pushing \(\mathrm{triv}_{p(i)}\)
1437	  forward from \(D(s_{p(i)})\) to \(D(r_i)\) for each \(i\). These pushed-forward
1438	  trivializations assemble into one trivialization of \(N\) over the cover algebra
1439	  \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i))\), and it intertwines the descent datum twisted by
1440	  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) with the canonical descent datum of \(N\) base-changed to the cover
1441	  algebra, by the defining property of the transition units on each factor of the twisted
1442	  double-overlap algebra \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i)) \otimes_A \prod_i \Gamma(X,D(r_i))\). Since
1443	  the cover algebra is faithfully flat over \(A\) (a finite family of basic opens covering the
1444	  affine \(X\)), uniqueness of descended modules identifies the module descended from
1445	  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) with \(N\) itself, so their classes in \(\operatorname{Pic}(A)\)
1446	  agree.
1447	\end{proof}

1449	\begin{definition}[The \v Cech--Picard descent homomorphism]
1450	  \label{def:cechPic_toPic}
1451	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic}
1452	  \leanok
1453	  For an affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\), the homomorphism of
1454	  groups
1455	  \[
1456	    \operatorname{toPic} \colon \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A), \qquad [\mathcal U,\gamma]
1457	    \mapsto \bigl(\text{class of the module descended from } \gamma|_{\mathcal W}\bigr),
1458	  \]
1459	  where \(\mathcal W\) is any finite basic refinement of \(\mathcal U\) and
1460	  \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\) is the cocycle obtained by restricting \(\gamma\) along
1461	  \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\).
1462	\end{definition}
1463	\begin{proof}
1464	  \leanok
1465	  The class of the descended module does not depend on the choice of finite basic refinement
1466	  \(\mathcal W\) of \(\mathcal U\): any two such refinements are dominated by a common one, along
1467	  which the two descended modules become identified. Nor does it depend on the representative
1468	  \((\mathcal U,\gamma)\) of the class \([\mathcal U,\gamma] \in \Pic(X)\): a further common
1469	  refinement of two cohomologous representing cocycles carries cohomologous restricted
1470	  cocycles, hence isomorphic descended modules. So \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is a well-defined
1471	  function; it is a homomorphism because descending along a common refinement is compatible
1472	  with the pointwise product of cocycles and with tensor product of the descended modules.
1473	\end{proof}

1475	\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the descent homomorphism]
1476	  \label{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective}
1477	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_injective}
1478	  \uses{def:cechPic_toPic, cor:cechPic_mk_eq_one}
1479	  \leanok
1480	  For every affine scheme \(X\), the descent homomorphism \(\operatorname{toPic} \colon
1481	  \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) of Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic} is injective.
1482	\end{theorem}
1483	\begin{proof}
1484	  \leanok
1485	  It suffices to show that a class \([\mathcal U,\gamma]\) with
1486	  \(\operatorname{toPic}[\mathcal U,\gamma] = 1\) is itself trivial. Represent
1487	  \([\mathcal U,\gamma]\) along a finite basic refinement \(\mathcal W \le \mathcal U\) as in
1488	  Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic}: since the module descended from \(\gamma|_{\mathcal W}\)
1489	  is isomorphic to \(A\), its twisted descent datum is isomorphic to the trivial descent datum
1490	  on \(\prod_i \Gamma(X,\mathcal W(i))\), so the transition units of \(\gamma\) restricted to
1491	  \(\mathcal W\) differ from those of the trivial cocycle by an index-wise coboundary. Since the
1492	  opens of \(\mathcal W\) refine those of \(\mathcal U\) and, member by member, cover them, this
1493	  coboundary glues, by the sheaf property of \(\struct X\), to a coboundary for \(\gamma\)
1494	  itself on \(\mathcal U\): \(\gamma = 1\) in \(\check H^1(\mathcal U)\). By
1495	  Corollary~\ref{cor:cechPic_mk_eq_one}, \([\mathcal U,\gamma] = 1\) in \(\Pic(X)\).
1496	\end{proof}

1498	\begin{theorem}[Surjectivity of the descent homomorphism]
1499	  \label{thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective}
1500	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_surjective}
1501	  \uses{def:cechPic_toPic, lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty, thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}
1502	  \leanok
1503	  For every affine scheme \(X\), the descent homomorphism \(\operatorname{toPic} \colon
1504	  \Pic(X) \to \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) is surjective.
1505	\end{theorem}
1506	\begin{proof}
1507	  \leanok
1508	  Let \(c \in \operatorname{Pic}(A)\) be represented by an invertible \(A\)-module \(N\). By
1509	  Lemma~\ref{lem:trivializingFamily_nonempty}, \(N\) admits a trivializing family, giving a
1510	  pointed cover \(\mathcal U_F\) together with the unit \v Cech \(1\)-cocycle \(\gamma_F\) of
1511	  Definition~\ref{def:trivializingFamily_cocycle}. Since \(X\) is affine, hence quasi-compact,
1512	  \(\mathcal U_F\) admits a finite basic refinement \(\mathcal W\). By
1513	  Theorem~\ref{thm:trivializingFamily_pic_cocycle}, \(\operatorname{toPic}[\mathcal
1514	  U_F,\gamma_F] = c\). As \(c\) was arbitrary, \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is surjective.
1515	\end{proof}

1517	\begin{theorem}[The \v Cech--Picard dictionary]
1518	  \label{thm:cechPicEquivPic}
1519	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic}
1520	  \uses{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective, thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective}
1521	  \leanok
1522	  For every affine scheme \(X\) with global ring \(A = \Gamma(X,\struct X)\), the descent
1523	  homomorphism of Definition~\ref{def:cechPic_toPic} is an isomorphism of groups
1524	  \[
1525	    \operatorname{toPic} \colon \Pic(X) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \operatorname{Pic}(A).
1526	  \]
1527	  In particular the definitional \v Cech Picard group \(\Pic(X)\) on pointed Zariski covers of
1528	  \(X\) is canonically isomorphic to mathlib's Picard group of invertible \(A\)-modules.
1529	\end{theorem}
1530	\begin{proof}
1531	  \leanok
1532	  \(\operatorname{toPic}\) is a bijective group homomorphism by
1533	  Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPic_toPic_injective} (injectivity) and
1534	  Theorem~\ref{thm:cechPic_toPic_surjective} (surjectivity), hence an isomorphism.
1535	\end{proof}
